audioDesc: Choose which card plays the live set. Optionally add a separate headphone card to pre-listen to other songs.
grantAccess: Grant access once so your output cards show their real names.
preListenDesc: Enable a separate headphone output for pre-listening.
sameCardWarn: Pre-listen and main are the same card — previews will be audible on the floor.
pickPreListen: Pick a pre-listen output to enable the headphone buttons.
cueHint: The play buttons in your library turn into a blue headphone {icon}. Click one and that track plays only on your pre-listen card — the dancers on the floor won't hear it.
cortinasDesc: Control how cortinas play during a live set.
cortinasNote: These settings only affect cortinas — the songs in between tandas. The snippet cut-off and fade out never apply to the tanda songs themselves.
snippetDesc: Play a short snippet of each cortina, then fade to the next tanda automatically.
snippetLenDesc: How long the cortina plays before fading.
fadeDesc: How long the cortina takes to fade into the next tanda, for both the auto-fade and the “Fade to next tanda” button.
levelingDesc: Even out volume across songs. Applied from a one-time background analysis of your library.
normalizeDesc: Pull loud songs down toward a consistent level so tandas don’t jump in volume.
targetDesc: Where songs are leveled to. Lower is quieter; raise the master to taste.
silenceDesc: Trim dead air at the start and end of each song and add a breath between tracks during a live set.
trimDesc: Skip complete silence at the very start and end of each song.
gapDesc: A short pause inserted before the next track plays in the live set.
trimEverywhereDesc: By default trimming shapes the live set only. Turn on to also trim when you preview a song from your library.
libraryDesc: Tidy how song titles read across Compás.
songNameOnlyDesc: Hide the orchestra, singer and year that are sometimes baked into a song’s title, leaving just the song name — everywhere songs appear: library, tandas, playlists and the live queue. The orchestra and singer still show on the line below.
songNameOnlyCortinasDesc: Cortinas are usually non-tango tracks whose titles don’t follow the “Orchestra – Song” pattern, so the clean-up can garble them. By default they keep their full title; turn on to tidy them as well.
collapseDesc: Start with every folder closed when you open the Library or the Tanda builder, so you can expand only the ones you need. Otherwise the top-level folders open automatically.
cortinasInFiltersDesc: Offer cortinas’ orchestras, singers, genres and years in the library’s filter dropdowns. When off, the dropdowns only list your dance music — cortinas still appear when you browse or search.
stripsIntro: Strips, on display only, the kinds of clutter that creep into title tags:
stripsOutro: Best-effort heuristics — a few oddly-tagged titles may not clean up perfectly. Your files and saved metadata are never changed.
signoff: Built for the people who make the night — the DJs spinning, the dancers in the ronda, everyone who keeps the floor alive. With all my heart. Enjoy.
contact: Bugs or suggestions? Reach out at {mail} or on Telegram {telegram}
title: Settings
subtitle: Audio routing, builder layout & appearance
themeDesc: Switch between the light and dark colour schemes.
textSizeDesc: Make everything in the app larger or smaller. Also adjustable with ⌘/Ctrl + and −.
tandaLayoutDesc: Show your saved tandas as compact tabs or as full-width big rows.
startDesc: New here, or just want a refresher?
tourDesc: Replay the welcome walkthrough of everything Compás can do.
filesDesc: Whether the edits you make in Compás also go into the song files on your computer.
writeTagsLabel: Also save changes to the music files
writeTagsDesc: When on, the song details you edit (title, orchestra, singer, year, album, genre) are also written into the file itself, so iTunes and other apps show the same names. When off, your changes stay inside Compás and nothing on your computer is touched.
writeTagsNote: Your music is never altered, only its labels. Orchestra and singer are saved together as “Orchestra - Singer”, the way most tango collections are already tagged. This also applies to Smart Organize and to editing several songs at once.
ctrlDesc: Play, fade and EQ from a DJ controller: Traktor Kontrol, Pioneer DDJ, Hercules and hundreds more.
ctrlNoneFound: No supported controller found. Connect it by USB, quit Traktor or any other DJ app, and try again.
ctrlNoMappingFound: No mapping found. If this is a DJ controller, pick its mapping.
ctrlDecks: Deck 1 controls the floor: play/pause, volume, mute and EQ (a locked set stays locked). Deck 2 controls the headphone pre-listen. A fader or knob only takes over once it passes the current level, so nothing jumps when you plug in.
ctrlCredit: Mappings are made by the {project} community ({version}, GPL). Compás downloads only the one your controller needs and keeps it on this computer, so it works offline.
ctrlErrNetwork: Couldn’t download the mapping. Check the internet connection and try again.
ctrlErrIntegrity: The downloaded mapping didn’t match the expected file, so it wasn’t used.
ctrlErrOpen: Couldn’t open the controller. Quit Traktor or any other app using it, then try again.
ctrlErrStart: The mapping couldn’t start on this controller.
ctrlOfferMsg: Compás can use your {device}. Download its mapping now? It’s small and only needed once.
